newsitem.title: USA: Medi-Ject reduces IPO price range.
newsitem.headline: Medi-Ject reduces IPO price range.

text.p: Medi-Ject Corp has cut the price for shares in its initial public offering, according to regulatory documents filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on Tuesday.
The Minneapolis company will offer 2.2 million shares in a range of $5.50 to $6 each. It had previously estimated the price at $8 to $10 each. Its shares will trade on the Nasdaq under the symbol.

Rodman & Renshaw is the lead underwriter of the offering. The drug delivery company focuses on injection systems that use, instead of a needle, a spring-powered device that injects a high pressure stream only seven-1000ths of an inch in diameter, helping people who have to self-administer drugs.
